correctness.rationale: The theorem concerns n≥3 and unit a mod n, with the ordinary unscaled Hessian of the explicitly specified Euler quadratic polynomial. The group-ring factor t^{-(a+1)}(t−1)(t^a−1)(1+t^{a+1}) was independently algebraically checked, including coincident shifts. Since a is a unit, multiplication by t^a−1 has precisely the augmentation ideal image, giving ker[(t−1)(t^a−1)]=ZN and coker A=Z⊕Z/n, with the stated exact sequence. For m=n/g odd, 1+t^{a+1} has g odd-length signed cycles, producing (Z/2)^{g−1} as kernel of the sequence; odd n splits, whereas even n is nonsplit by exact F2 nullity g (one fewer even torsion factor than the split case). For m even, the signed cycles give free Z^g and torsion injects into Z/n, hence cyclic; the integer kernel basis B_0,A_r has Gram determinant nm^g/4 while Fourier nonzero eigenvalues multiply to n²m^g/8, giving torsion n/2 and free rank g+1. An independently written SymPy SNF checker verified every admissible pair 3≤n≤22 plus six higher cases (154), with extra mod-2 and pseudodeterminant checks for small n; these finite checks corroborate the infinite proof, not replace it.

value.rationale: The Euler quadratic form is a natural representation-theoretic lattice invariant of isolated cyclic quotient surface stacks. Its exact integral cokernel and radical are finer than rational rank and directly compare canonical Euler data across all unit-weight actions. The complete invariant factors exhibit a genuine parity/gcd phase transition, including an infinite exceptional free-rank jump and a cyclic-vs-elementary 2-torsion dichotomy. These require substantive integer-extension and covolume analysis, rather than relabeling a textbook computation or reading off a known finite table. The result has self-contained mathematical use as exact integral Euler-lattice data, without claiming a new geometric existence theorem.
residual_risks: This is a focused integral-lattice classification, not a Hilbert-scheme dimension or smoothness theorem.
The mathematical significance is structural, not supported by a proved downstream application.
